convoLines.text: "This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
The ground remembers.
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
"I should get back to it."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Another crack. The telling doesn't hold together anymore.
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
Another pass over the same ground. Somebody's being careful. Careful people leave cleaner trails — and cleaner trails are still trails.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the stinging nettle patch past the treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Pamela is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Ethel doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"I oil boots on rest days. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I have been lying about my age — I'm younger than I look!"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Ji. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask? Good talking."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Pamela owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Alright. Catch you later."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Can we talk?" Ethel sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you heard what they're calling Nightlight? Ethel is pushing 'Ugly-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.'"
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I rinse the cup twice instead."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Wild Strawberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up? You know?"
"Good question." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said you don't recognize the person in your head anymore. Still a stranger to yourself?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Yeah? What's up? I hope that helps."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Yara — The Cache, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I tried the Wild Strawberry like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
Ji has an edge today — something curdled.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Cache. They just... took Yara. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
